correctness.rationale: Direct propagation gives \(p_2=(c^2/2,s^2,c^2/2)\) and \(p_3=(c^4/2,(1-c^4)/2,(1-c^4)/2,c^4/2)\). Shannon entropy on three or four accessible sites is maximized exactly by uniformity, yielding the stated unique angles on \([0,\pi/2]\). Fresh independent state propagation reproduced exact numerical uniformity at both angles and the Hadamard deficits. At one step the two position probabilities are one half for every angle, establishing earliest strict failure at step two. The frozen verifier was read and independently propagates the same walk.
correctness.risk: The theorem is only about position Shannon entropy at steps one through three for the cited initial state and coin convention.

originality.rationale: The original paper says the Hadamard coin has maximum measurement entropy and supports the discussion with much larger-step plots. The erratum does not alter that conclusion. Ide-Konno-Machida later state that numerical results suggest entropy increases to \(\pi/4\) and decreases after it for any \(n\). The audited exact two- and three-step formulas directly contradict that universal finite-time suggestion, while targeted searches found no prior exact optimizer angles or earliest-counterexample statement.

value.rationale: This is the earliest boundary test of a published universal finite-time entropy statement, and the corrected angles attain the absolute information-theoretic maximum by uniformizing every accessible position. The correction is mathematically motivated and directly relevant to finite-time quantum-walk spreading.
value.risk: No large-time or asymptotic optimizer claim is made.

final_claim: For the cited symmetric one-dimensional quantum walk, the unique position-entropy maximizers are \(\theta_2^*=\arcsin(1/\sqrt3)\) at two steps and \(\theta_3^*=\arccos(2^{-1/4})\) at three steps, attaining uniform distributions and entropies \(\log_2 3\) and two respectively. The Hadamard angle is strictly suboptimal at both times, and two steps is the earliest nontrivial failure of the published finite-time Hadamard-maximality statement.
limitations: Only the cited symmetric initial state, coin family and steps one through three are classified.
Position Shannon entropy, not coin-position entanglement entropy, is optimized.
